//: Verdigris · CANDLELIT STONE. A painted dark-fantasy scene: a gothic castle of
//1: black-green stone in a mountain pass, its windows and gates lit a pale
//2: witch-green, a stone bridge over green-lit water, a dragon in the olive sky,
//3: the sun a pale yellow-green glow at the top centre, two gargoyles on the
//4: left cliff. No upstream palette — every role is sampled from the picture, and
//5: `tokens` names each after what it is there so the mapping stays traceable.
//6: THE source for every shell surface (quickshell/: bar, launcher, OSD, power
//7: menu); theme.lua still owns WINDOW chrome and CI cross-checks it against this.
//8: Two-tone rule, gothic edition: WITCHLIGHT (the gates' green) is the frame —
//9: island rims, window border, lock ring, btop boxes — BONE (the window light,
//10: desaturated) is every readout, and the SUN's pale yellow-green is the
//11: launcher, the one lit thing that is not green-white. This is the first green
//12: theme, and the risk with green is reading sickly or muddy, so the readouts
//13: are PALE: the window glow lifted to bone-green, not a terminal green. warn is
//14: the olive sky saturated a little so it reads as a state; urgent is a dull
//15: ember — nothing in the picture is red, so it is chosen for contrast on
//16: `surface`, not scenery; `ok` is the witchlight LIT, as glacier's ok is lit
//17: ice, so ok reads as more light, not a foreign green. readoutBright is the
//18: lit windows' white, so the active workspace is an emissive bone lozenge
//19: (modules/Workspaces.qml). The bridge moss and the dragon are the quiet
//20: family — `dim` and `dormant` — printed UP for contrast: as painted they read
//21: 2.4:1 and 2.9:1 on `surface`, and every surface that carries them is stone.
name: verdigris
//tokens: What in the picture -> role, so a palette bump stays traceable. `urgent` has no token: there is no red in the picture, it is state (an ember). `sky` is scenery that became state because it already sits where state needs to be: the one olive-gold thing in a green picture is something pending.
//contrast: Measured on the three surfaces that carry type (WCAG, sRGB blend): `surface`; the bar island — fill #0f1210 at 0.82 over the olive-grey strip the bar covers (#4e563e, composite ~#1a1e18); the launcher window — `ground` at 0.88 over the picture's centre (#435341 → ~#1b1e18). dim 3.6 / 4.1 / 4.1, dormant 5.0 / 5.6 / 5.6, frame 5.4 / 6.1 / 6.1, readout 10.4 / 11.8 / 11.8, readoutBright 13.2 / 15.0 / 14.9, warn 7.4 / 8.4 / 8.4, ok 9.2 / 10.4 / 10.4, urgent 3.9 / 4.4 / 4.4, text 10.7 / 12.1 / 12.1, launcher 11.5 / 13.1 / 13.0. `ground` on `readout` (the lozenge's digit) 12.6:1, `ground` on `frame` 6.5:1; the launcher's selected row (launcher on its own 18% tint) holds 8.0:1.
//effects: Candlelight, not neon: no text glow — candlelight does not bloom. The panel texture is a vignette — black closing in from the corners of every pane, clear at the centre: stone lit from the middle — and it is the signature. 0.5 over the kind's resting 0.35: the island fill is near-black at 0.82 over an olive blur, and the vignette has to show against a fill that dark.
//bar: Bar identity. Stone panels: near-black islands at 0.82 — the strip the bar covers is the olive sky at the top of the picture (#4e563e), LIGHTER than most of it, so the fill has to be dark and fairly opaque where harbor's could be a silhouette — with a 1px witchlight rim at 40%, 6px corners (a gothic arch is not a round corner; 6 keeps it from gruvbox's 4), no accent line, and a FAINT witchlight bloom (0.12 over 16px): light leaking from a gate, the one bloom the theme allows. The fill (#0f1210) sits a shade UNDER `ground`: at 18% show-through it lands the composite at ~#1a1e18 — `dim` 4.1:1, `dormant` 5.6:1, `urgent` 4.4:1, `readout` 11.8:1, `text` 12.1:1.
//launcher: Launcher identity: a 1px sun frame (the pale yellow-green, the one lit thing that is not green-white) around dark stone (0.88), 6px window, 4px input + rows — the chips' corner. The launcher is the one surface that covers the bar, so it is the one shell surface that wears the sun: its frame and its selected row.
//osd: OSD identity: a slab, not a pill (as inkwash's is) — 6px corners, the one radius, a 1px witchlight frame, a bone track (the readout), 0.88 so the stone still shows faintly under it.
//session: Power-menu identity: 6px tiles with a 1px witchlight edge at 45%, over a 0.75 rock scrim — the castle stays visible behind the menu, sunk into shadow.
//wallpaper: Shared by hyprlock.conf (brightness) and sddm/Main.qml (1 - brightness scrim). 0.55 with an 8px blur, the dark themes' resting numbers: the picture is already night, and the lock stack sits over the dark cliff on the left, so it needs no extra dimming.
